capabilities: Define test rules as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in a test folder
Check note existence, link resolution, backlink counts, frontmatter fields, and source links
Rerun only tests affected by edited, renamed, or deleted notes
Show pass/fail results and failure reasons in a sidebar view
Get plain-language help interpreting failures via an optional OpenAI-compatible endpoint
disambiguation: Not a statistics or data-regression tool; 'regression' here means re-running pass/fail tests to catch vault decay.
extras: The optional AI assistance sends data to an external endpoint, but only when manually triggered; the plugin otherwise runs fully locally and never modifies notes. Manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it because vaults 'rot quietly' and there was no way to define what a healthy vault looks like and check it automatically.
problem: Vaults degrade silently: renamed notes break links, required frontmatter fields get forgotten, and nothing flags it until much later.

relations.evidence: lets you connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (provider URL, model, API key)

summary: Vault test runner that checks notes, links, backlinks, and frontmatter against Markdown-defined rules and reports pass/fail results.
